sentences.text: Sonselasuchus had a bipedal stance, a pronounced pubic boot, large orbital openings, and jaws lacking teeth.
Scientists propose that its snout was covered by a keratinous beak comparable to those of turtles and birds.
More than 950 isolated bones representing at least 36 individuals were recovered from a single quarry.
Fossils of the taxon come from the Chinle Formation of Arizona, dating to the Late Triassic Norian age.
All specimens derive from the Kaye Quarry, which Tom Kaye uncovered in 2014.
The genus and species were formally described by Elliott Armour Smith and Christian A. Sidor in 2026.
Juvenile individuals appear to have moved on all fours, while adults shifted to an upright, two-legged gait.
It belongs to the poposauroid superfamily and is placed within the family Shuvosauridae.
Phylogenetic studies locate it in the Shuvosauridae clade, though its exact relationship to Effigia and Shuvosaurus remains unresolved.
Sonselasuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
